question: What stage will the BCP have reached in disposing of Ueno Bank's assets and liabilities before November 28, 2026?

calls.reasoning: BCP (Schreiner, 12 Nov) announced plan: exclusion balance in ~8-10 days, then a licitación of asset+deposit lotes to several local banks, transfer 'by end of month at the latest' (~27 Nov, right at the cutoff). As of 15 Nov Diario HOY reports the transfer mechanism still 'under study', no dates or entities confirmed, contingent on asset clean-up and final valuation. Central-bank resolution timelines usually slip, and a BCP legal manager was arrested on 16 Nov, which could slow the legal work. So a tender announcement within ~11 days is near a coin flip. Naming a recipient needs an award or direct designation, and an award typically follows tender close and bid evaluation, so it is least likely. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
sources: WebSearch results: La Nacion 12 Nov (lotes plan), economia.com.py, ADN Digital snippets, elbuentono.com.mx (BCP legal manager arrest 16 Nov)
calls.dossier:
- 2 Nov 2026: BCP board Resolution No. 1, Acta 49, opened the Ueno Bank resolution under Ley 2334/2003; announced 3 Nov (FIX SCR, ABC Color).
- 12 Nov: Schreiner said about USD 600M of sound assets were identified, more than Ueno's pension-sector liabilities (IPS about USD 516M). Plan: exclusion balance in ~8-10 days, then a licitación of asset+deposit lotes to several local banks, avoiding a single 'megabanco'; transfer 'by end of month at the latest' (~15 days from 12 Nov) (La Nacion, HOY, economia.com.py, 12-13 Nov).
- Statutory exclusion-balance deadline is 15 days from the start of the process (about 17 Nov if calendar days); officials said they were trying to shorten it.
- 15 Nov, Diario HOY: FGD director Jose Maciel said the asset-and-liability transfer mechanism is 'under study', pending asset clean-up and a final patrimonial evaluation; 'no dates or entities confirmed'.
- 14 Nov (Wikipedia timeline): a BCP director said banks 'could' assume Ueno deposits via transfer of assets and liabilities.
- FGD advance paid to about 1.81M depositors by 12 Nov (about USD 644M); CDA registration platform opened 12 Nov.
- Banks named so far (Atlas, Basa, Nacion Argentina, Familiar, GNB, Itau, Bancop, Interfisa, Solar, Sudameris, Continental, Zeta, plus some financieras) are payment agents and account-opening venues only, excluded by the fine print (Revista Mercado 10 Nov; La Nacion 5 Nov).
- 16 Nov: BCP legal manager Aldo Rodriguez turned himself in after an arrest warrant over the Ueno irregularities; 27 executives charged. Possible institutional distraction or delay.
- The ABC Color communique compilation (as fetched) lists items only up to 5 Nov, with no tender communique.
- Status quo as of 16 Nov: no tender launched, no recipient named.
- Resolves off BCP or intervention-team public announcements made on or before 27 Nov (Paraguay time); payment-agent bank lists, intent statements, and completion of the exclusion balance do not count.
- Event window: 2 Nov -> 27 Nov 2026 per the criteria; as of 16 Nov about 56% elapsed (about 11 days remain).
- Searched but not found: any published pliego or tender date, any list of bidding banks, any bridge-bank or trust (fideicomiso) designation, any prediction market (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi: none found).
- Base-rate note: officially announced timelines in emergency bank resolutions often slip by weeks. A purchase-and-assumption award usually follows the tender launch by days to weeks, but direct board designation without a public tender is possible.
calls.reference_class: Bank resolutions under Paraguay's Ley 2334 and LatAm central-bank purchase-and-assumption resolutions: time from intervention to tender launch and to naming acquirers, compared with official announced timelines

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of Nov 15: no tender launched, no recipient named; FGD director said the transfer mechanism is 'under study', no entities confirmed, timelines undefined. BCP president Schreiner (Nov 12) said the exclusion balance would take 8-10 days, then a tender in lots, with transfers 'a más tardar a fin de mes'. The window closes Nov 27, before month-end, so even an on-schedule plan puts the award near or past the cutoff, while a tender launch around Nov 22-26 is plausible. The case is large (8-9% of the system), the lots go to several banks and forensic issues remain, so slippage risk is high. An invitation-only process might also only surface at the award. Markets: no Polymarket/Manifold market per the harness title search; I did not search Kalshi or bookmakers myself and assumed none (not verified).
calls.dossier:
- Nov 2-3 2026: BCP board starts the Ueno Bank resolution under Ley 2334/03; statutory exclusion-balance closing deadline is 15 days from the start (background; business vs calendar days unclear). Source: question background, bcp.gov.py communiqué.
- Nov 12 (La Nación, Diario HOY, facundoquiroga.com): Schreiner says about USD 600M of sound assets; exclusion balance in 8-10 days, then a licitación in lots to several local banks to avoid a 'megabanco'; transfers 'a más tardar, a fin de mes'. Other reporting gives about 15 days total from Nov 12 (around Nov 27).
- Nov 15 (Diario HOY): FGD director José Maciel says the asset/liability transfer mechanism is 'under study', pending final asset evaluations; 'no entities confirmed'; timelines undefined.
- Nov 15 (Infobae/EFE): BCP director Pedro Acosta says assets and liabilities will be organized into lots and auctioned; uncovered depositors must 'wait the result of the balance of exclusion'. No dates, no banks named.
- ABC Color compilation of BCP communiqués (checked Nov 16): no communiqué on a licitación, pliego, lots or a named recipient; only FGD payout and payment-agent bank items (these do not count).
- Ueno is about 8-9% of the banking system, so the lots must go to several banks and absorption is limited by each bank's capital. There are related-party and fraud-investigation complications.
- Searched for a pliego/bases/convocatoria for the Ueno tender: none found as of Nov 16. Searched for Paraguayan precedents of Ley 2334 exclusion-balance transfers with timelines: none found. The Ley 2334 PDF on bcp.gov.py returned 403.
- Resolution instrument: public BCP or intervention-team announcements on or before Nov 27 (Paraguay time). Payment-agent banks, Ueno Casa de Bolsa and the fund manager do not count; statements of intent and completion of the exclusion balance alone do not count.
- Event window: Nov 2/3 (process start) -> Nov 27 2026 per the criteria; as of Nov 16 about 55% of the window since the process began has elapsed, with 11 days left.
- Status quo: no tender launched and no recipient named.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket or Manifold (harness search).
calls.reference_class: Latin American statutory bank resolutions with exclusion-balance plus purchase-and-assumption tenders where officials announced a 2-3 week timetable; official timetables slip by a week or more in roughly half of cases

calls.reasoning: As of Nov 15-16 no tender or recipient is public; FGD director says the transfer mechanism is still under study with no dates or banks. Schreiner (Nov 12) projected the exclusion balance in 8-10 days (~Nov 20-22) followed by a tender of lots; some reports put tender+transfer at ~15 days (~Nov 27), right at the deadline. Officials' own timelines for complex multi-lot resolutions of an 8-9%-of-system bank usually slip, and invitation-only processes may not be public before an award. The upside case is real: IPS and pension-fund pressure, and the BCP has publicly committed to the schedule. Naming a recipient within 11 days requires the full sequence to finish. No human prediction market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).
calls.dossier:
- Nov 2 2026: BCP board (Res. 1, Acta 49) opened resolution of Ueno Bank under Ley 2334/2003; announced Nov 3 (FIX SCR; ABC).
- Nov 5-12: FGD advance of up to 40 minimum wages paid to ~1.81M depositors (~USD 644M) (Hoy Digital, Nov 15).
- Nov 11 (La Nación): BCP preparing a second stage to raise coverage to 75 minimum wages; assets and liabilities to be offered to FGD-contributing entities.
- Nov 12 (La Nación, Diario HOY, Perfil): Schreiner says ~USD 600M of sound assets identified; exclusion balance in ~8-10 more days, then a licitación of lots to several local banks to avoid a 'megabanco'; some reports put tender and transfer at ~15 days from Nov 12.
- Nov 15 (Diario HOY): FGD director José Maciel says the transfer mechanism is 'under study' and awaits closing of accounting verifications; no dates or banks confirmed.
- ABC Color compilation of BCP communiqués (checked Nov 16): entries cover Nov 3-5 payout logistics only; nothing on a tender, lots or recipient banks.
- Ley 2334: interventors form the exclusion balance 'immediately'; transfers to one or more solvent entities through competitive processes; no day count for the auction; guarantee payout within 15 days, extendable by 15; transfer documents formalized within 90 days.
- Ueno is ~8-9% of the banking system; multi-lot split across several banks planned.
- Status quo as of Nov 16: no tender public, no recipient named.
- Resolves off BCP / intervention-team public announcements reported by credible media, not off statements of intent; payment-agent banks do not count; Ueno Casa de Bolsa and AFPISA are excluded.
- Event window: Nov 2 -> Nov 27 2026 (Paraguay time) per the criteria; as of Nov 16 ~56% elapsed (11 days remain).
- Searched, not found: any BCP publication of tender terms, a list of invited banks, a bridge-bank plan, any prediction market on this.
- Both directions: public pressure from the IPS (USD 516M at Ueno) and pension funds, plus the BCP's stated schedule, push toward speed; the size and complexity of the bank, the multi-lot design, and pending verification push toward delay.
calls.reference_class: Announced official timelines for multi-step bank resolution transactions (exclusion balance -> tender -> award) in Latin American P&A-style resolutions; officials' self-set deadlines frequently slip by weeks

calls.reasoning: As of Nov 16, nothing qualifies: there is no tender and no named recipient, and the FGD says the transfer mechanism is still under study. The BCP's own plan puts the exclusion balance around Nov 20-22, then a tender of lots, with transfer 'by end of month at the latest'. That plan lands right at or after the Nov 27 cutoff. Official timelines in a large multi-lot resolution like this usually slip, and the arrest of the BCP's legal manager adds friction. The status quo therefore stays the most likely outcome. If the BCP runs a restricted process, it may only become public when the award is announced. That skips the 'tender only' stage, so I put somewhat more weight on 'recipient named' than the runs did. No human prediction market was found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs did not dispute any material facts. All three report that as of Nov 15-16 there was no tender and no recipient, cite the same Nov 12 Schreiner schedule and the Nov 15 statement from FGD director Maciel, and found no market. The differences are judgment calls: how much the schedule slips, and whether a restricted process would be announced before its award. I had no web access on this run, so I worked only from the dossiers. Under Ley 2334, transfers go 'to one or more solvent entities through competitive processes', and such deals are often announced already done with the recipient named. I therefore moved some weight from 'tender only' to 'recipient named'. The status quo stays the modal outcome because the cutoff falls before the stated end-of-month target.

disagreements.claim: Whether the BCP schedule (exclusion balance Nov 20-22, then tender) will hold within the window
disagreements.verdict: Slippage is likely given the bank's size, the ongoing fraud investigation and the legal manager's arrest; the status quo stays the modal outcome

disagreements.claim: Whether a restricted or invitation-only tender would be publicized before an award
disagreements.verdict: Plausibly not; this moves some mass to 'recipient named' conditional on any action

disagreements.claim: Whether the 15-day statutory exclusion-balance deadline counts calendar or business days
disagreements.verdict: Could not be settled without the text of the law; the effect is small because completing the balance does not count either way
